content.text:
The change adds four static PWA-related tags to `index.html`:
- `<link rel="manifest" href="/manifest.webmanifest" />`
- `<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/icon.svg" />`
- `<meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-capable" content="yes" />`
- `<meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style" content="black-translucent" />`

Analysis per method:

**Phase 1 — Entry points/sinks:** None. All four additions are static markup with hard-coded string values. No attacker-influenceable data reaches any sink; the only "sink" (browser rendering of `href`/`content`) receives constants baked into the source file.

**Phase 2 — Data flow:** No variables, no interpolation, no user input, no template rendering. The referenced paths (`/manifest.webmanifest`, `/icon.svg`) are same-origin relative URLs served as static assets.

**Phase 2b/2c — High-miss patterns:**
- No parser/validator changes.
- No logging/telemetry sinks.
- No IaC / CI/CD trigger changes.
- No allowlist, grant, identity-mapping, or registry changes.
- `apple-mobile-web-app-capable=yes` + `black-translucent` are standard PWA hints — they change how iOS chromes the page when saved to home screen, not any security boundary. No cookie/storage isolation change.
- Manifest file itself is not part of the diff; if it later contains untrusted values that would be a separate review.

No source→sink path exists in this diff. No findings.
